title: Implement hub provider grabber layer for usage, limits, and availability telemetry
description: Build the pluggable collection layer that gathers provider/model telemetry for the hub model routing table. This includes provider APIs, usage and limits collection, capacity snapshots, spend tracking, and manual override channels so model advice stays fresh and locally informed.
non_goals: Do not require every provider to expose the same API surface
Do not require cohort sharing in this batch
verification_requirements: Verify grabbers are pluggable per provider
Verify usage/limits/cost snapshots can flow into the routing table
Verify manual overrides are supported when provider telemetry is incomplete

review_history.summary: Lug concept is clear and the non-goals are well-scoped. Three gaps filled in this cycle: (1) grabber_interface_contract added — builder now has exact function signatures (collect, supports_live_api, manual_override_path), file naming convention, manual-override schema, and refresh policy; (2) dependency on implementation-hub-model-routing-table-v1 made explicit (registry.json must exist before grabbers can write to it); (3) three runnable acceptance tests added. Ready for builder to claim after routing-table ships.
recommendations: Start with a manual.py grabber (supports_live_api=False) as a smoke test before building live API grabbers — validates the interface without requiring credentials.
provider-usage.json should be a JSONL or timestamped JSON array so history accumulates — builder should treat it as an append-log, not an overwrite.
Build anthropic.py grabber first since it is the primary provider for this project.

workflow.handoff_reason: Implementer review + gap fill complete. Builder can claim after routing-table ships.

grabber_interface_contract._note: Each provider grabber is a Python module in hub/model-routing/grabbers/{provider}.py

required_functions.collect() -> dict: Returns a snapshot dict with keys: provider, collected_at, models (list), availability (str), rate_limit_state (str), remaining_capacity (int or null), window_reset_at (ISO-8601 or null), estimated_unit_cost (dict: model_id -> float), observed_errors (list). Must not raise — return error_state on failure.
required_functions.supports_live_api() -> bool: Returns True if this grabber can call a live provider API. Returns False for manual-override-only grabbers.
required_functions.manual_override_path() -> str: Returns path to the manual override JSON file for this provider, relative to hub/model-routing/. E.g. 'overrides/anthropic.json'.

manual_override_schema._note: Placed at hub/model-routing/overrides/{provider}.json when live API unavailable

fields.models: list of model entries matching collect() models output
fields.reason: why manual override is in use

refresh_policy.on_demand: Hub operator calls grab.py --provider=anthropic to refresh one provider
refresh_policy.scheduled: grab.py --all runs all grabbers and merges into registry.json
refresh_policy.staleness_threshold: 24 hours — grabber outputs older than this are flagged in routing table advice

acceptance_tests.description: At least one grabber module exists
acceptance_tests.command: ls hub/model-routing/grabbers/*.py 2>/dev/null && echo PASS || echo FAIL
acceptance_tests.expected: PASS — at least one grabber .py file present

acceptance_tests.command: python3 -c "import importlib.util, sys; spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('g', list(__import__('glob').glob('hub/model-routing/grabbers/*.py'))[0]); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m); assert hasattr(m,'collect') and hasattr(m,'supports_live_api') and hasattr(m,'manual_override_path'); print('PASS')" 2>/dev/null || echo FAIL
acceptance_tests.expected: PASS — collect(), supports_live_api(), manual_override_path() all present

acceptance_tests.description: Registry.json is updated by grabber output
acceptance_tests.command: test -f hub/model-routing/registry.json && python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('hub/model-routing/registry.json')); assert 'providers' in d or 'models' in d; print('PASS')" || echo FAIL
acceptance_tests.expected: PASS — registry.json exists and has providers or models key
